scenes.tts: How do you count packets when the bumps blur together?
scenes.visual: A histogram whose bumps have smeared into one another, with the question on screen.
scenes.narration: How do you count packets when the bumps blur together?

scenes.tts: You want one number: the mean quantal content. It is the average number of packets one impulse releases.
scenes.caption: You want one number: the mean quantal content, m. It is the average number of packets one impulse releases.
scenes.visual: Label: mean quantal content, m = average packets per impulse. Small note: not the m of the sodium gates.
scenes.narration: You want one number: the mean quantal content, m. It is the average number of packets one impulse releases.

scenes.tts: There are two ways to get it. They rest on different assumptions, and that is the point.
scenes.visual: Two columns appear, headed direct method and failure method.
scenes.narration: There are two ways to get it. They rest on different assumptions, and that is the point.

scenes.tts: The first is direct. Every response is a whole number of packets.
scenes.visual: A covered jar on a scale; readings come in whole-coin steps.
scenes.narration: The first is direct. Every response is a whole number of packets.

scenes.tts: So the average response, divided by the size of one packet, gives the average count.
scenes.visual: On screen: m = mean EPP (failures included) / mean miniature.
scenes.narration: So the average response, divided by the size of one packet, gives the average count.

scenes.tts: Count each failure as a response of zero.
scenes.visual: The failures are added to the average as zeros, shown as empty readings.
scenes.narration: Count each failure as a response of zero.

scenes.tts: This needs evoked packets the same size as miniatures, and packets that add linearly.
scenes.visual: Two assumption tags under the direct method: evoked packets = miniatures; linear adding.
scenes.narration: This needs evoked packets the same size as miniatures, and packets that add linearly.

scenes.tts: The second way sounds like a trick. It counts only the failures.
scenes.visual: The failure-method column lights up.
scenes.narration: The second way sounds like a trick. It counts only the failures.

scenes.tts: Picture the terminal as a row of release sites, like tiny lamps.
scenes.visual: A row of 100 tiny unlit lamps across the frame, labelled release sites (N).
scenes.narration: Picture the terminal as a row of release sites, like tiny lamps.

scenes.tts: On each impulse, every site has a small chance to flash, independently of the others.
scenes.visual: An impulse arrives; a few scattered lamps flash. Label: each site, small chance p, the same on every trial.
scenes.narration: On each impulse, every site has a small chance to flash, independently of the others.

scenes.tts: A flash is one packet released.
scenes.visual: One flashing lamp is circled. Label: flash = 1 packet.
scenes.narration: A flash is one packet released.

scenes.tts: A failure means every single site stayed dark.
scenes.visual: An impulse arrives and no lamp flashes. A counter labelled all-dark trials ticks up.
scenes.narration: A failure means every single site stayed dark.

scenes.tts: The more packets released on average, the rarer an all-dark trial becomes.
scenes.visual: Many trials play fast. A slider raises the average; the all-dark counter slows.
scenes.narration: The more packets released on average, the rarer an all-dark trial becomes.

scenes.tts: Each site stays dark with chance one minus p. The sites are independent, so multiply those chances together.
scenes.visual: Each lamp shows 1 − p. They multiply: (1 − p) × (1 − p) × … = (1 − p)^N.
scenes.narration: Each site stays dark with chance one minus p. The sites are independent, so multiply those chances together.

scenes.tts: When p is small, that product comes very close to e to the minus m.
scenes.caption: When p is small, that product comes very close to e^(−m).
scenes.visual: On screen: (1 − p)^N ≈ e^(−N × p) = e^(−m).
scenes.narration: When p is small, that product comes very close to e^(−m).

scenes.tts: So the fraction of failures fixes the average count. The formula is on screen.
scenes.visual: On screen: P(failure) ≈ e^(−m), so m = −ln(failures / trials). Assumption tag: independent sites, small chances, the same conditions on every trial pooled.
scenes.narration: So the fraction of failures fixes the average count. The formula is on screen.

scenes.tts: Suppose an impulse releases one packet on average. How often does it release nothing at all?
scenes.visual: The lamp row with the average set to one packet. The question on screen.
scenes.narration: Suppose an impulse releases one packet on average. How often does it release nothing at all?

scenes.tts: More than a third of the time. The number is on screen.
scenes.visual: On screen: m = 1, fraction of failures = e^(−1) = 0.37.
scenes.narration: More than a third of the time. The number is on screen.

scenes.tts: The average is pulled up by trials that release two or three.
scenes.visual: Trials with two and three flashes highlight beside the many dark ones.
scenes.narration: The average is pulled up by trials that release two or three.

scenes.tts: Why bother with two methods? Because the failure method never uses the size of a packet.
scenes.visual: Side by side: the direct method uses q; the failure method does not, with q crossed out.
scenes.narration: Why bother with two methods? Because the failure method never uses the size of a packet.

scenes.tts: If evoked packets differed in size from miniatures, the direct method would go wrong. The failure method would not, as long as failures can still be told apart from noise.
scenes.visual: The direct-method tag 'evoked packets = miniatures' flashes red; the failure method stays green, with a small tag: reliable detection of failures.
scenes.narration: If evoked packets differed in size from miniatures, the direct method would go wrong. The failure method would not, as long as failures can still be told apart from noise.

scenes.tts: So when the two estimates agree, that agreement supports two things.
scenes.visual: The two estimates slide together and match.
scenes.narration: So when the two estimates agree, that agreement supports two things.

scenes.tts: That evoked and spontaneous packets are the same units, and that release behaves like many small, independent chances.
scenes.visual: Two check marks: same units; many small, independent chances.
scenes.narration: That evoked and spontaneous packets are the same units, and that release behaves like many small, independent chances.

scenes.tts: In a made-up recording of two hundred stimuli, the two estimates both come out near one packet.
scenes.visual: Worked problem on screen: 200 stimuli, q = 0.40 mV, mean EPP = 0.40 mV, 74 failures. Direct m = 1.00; failure m = −ln(74/200) = 0.99.
scenes.narration: In a made-up recording of two hundred stimuli, the two estimates both come out near one packet.

scenes.tts: The same reasoning predicts how many trials release each number of packets. That is the Poisson distribution.
scenes.visual: The histogram returns. Predicted trial counts from P(k) = e^(−m) × m^k / k! are drawn as the area under each bump.
scenes.narration: The same reasoning predicts how many trials release each number of packets. That is the Poisson distribution.

scenes.tts: Each site's chance must be small. Small, not equal.
scenes.visual: The lamp row shows sites with different small chances, labelled small, not equal.
scenes.narration: Each site's chance must be small. Small, not equal.

scenes.tts: Now restore normal calcium. The total release becomes large, tens of packets on every impulse.
scenes.visual: Calcium rises. Many lamps across the long row flash on each impulse; the total count is large.
scenes.narration: Now restore normal calcium. The total release becomes large, tens of packets on every impulse.

scenes.tts: Failures vanish, so there is nothing left to count. Low calcium is what makes failures common enough to measure.
scenes.visual: The all-dark counter stops at zero. Label: low calcium makes failures measurable.
scenes.narration: Failures vanish, so there is nothing left to count. Low calcium is what makes failures common enough to measure.

scenes.tts: Low calcium is not just convenient. It makes the chances small and failures common, as the mathematics needs.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: the zeros reveal the average, but only when release chances are small, as in low calcium.
scenes.narration: Low calcium is not just convenient. It makes the chances small and failures common, as the mathematics needs.
